summary: Phase 1 implements FR-1 and FR-2 exactly as planned. The guard predicate, the FAIL line, and the PASS line match the plan and the spec word for word. FAIL lines go to stderr, one per hit; the PASS line goes to stdout. The --track scope, the usage error with exit 2, the archive exclusion, and the hits file removal all hold. Catalog A8 keeps its heading and Guard line and names the accepted set. All 14 cases pass, the sweep passes with 93 plans, the single-track check passes, and the catalog test exits 0. No other live caller of the guard breaks; doctor.sh step 2 now passes and step 4 is untouched. The closeout rule stays a separate installed rule.
nonblocking_findings: N1: The predicate '^- \[[^ ~xb]\] ' does not match a marker of two or more characters, so '- [xx] task' and '- []' pass the guard. The base guard accepted them too, so this is not a regression. Test-strategy finding F3 records it as a known residual for Review B.

N2: The guard comment at tests/orchestrator_marker_vocabulary.sh lines 32 to 40 now names the closeout rule (no [ ] or [~] task at archive), which is an installed-role rule and stays outside this track. The comment states it; nothing enforces it here.
